observations.summary: The firm explains how a multi-year inspection record can inform maintenance decisions and puts the presenters and their project in view.
The indexed caption identifies staff measuring a culvert in North Reading and names the recorded dimensions and water depth. June 2026 is the fieldwork date.
Its Hobart example traces a field inspection form and photos through Survey123 into GIS dashboards used by city staff.
The firm features a stormwater engineer discussing flood risk, post-storm conditions and how trusted infrastructure data informs decisions.
The Topeka case shows the facility ID as the link between basin-level GIS inventory and the city's Cityworks system.
The indexed training demonstrates GIS for inspection tracking, field notes, asset condition and maintenance planning. The chapters give the viewer a practical sequence.
RJN's San Antonio case explains how the updated GIS connects storm sewer records with condition assessment, inspection video and risk information for maintenance planning.

payload.performance_read: Public examples show the use of field photos, inspection explainers and map-to-maintenance stories. Dates and engagement are too sparse for a comparison of formats or a reliable momentum call.

tests.idea: Show a one-inlet proof card in a private prime interview. Hook: “Can your reviewer find the right photo from the map?” Link one synthetic asset ID to its geometry, image index and inspection record. Show how an unconfirmed downstream connection is assigned for follow-up
tests.success_metric: primes who share a schema or identify a basin for a scoped inventory review

tests.idea: Try a one-basin scope sheet. Show the source records accepted, asset count cap, sample exception register and handoff to the prime's reviewer. Ask what their field team needs to verify before desktop QA
tests.success_metric: qualified partners who can supply records and name an acceptance owner and deadline
